issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may not make an order prejudicial to a person without giving that person an opportunity to be heard, even when the person has not yet been summoned as an accused.
material_facts: A complainant filed a complaint and sought a police investigation; the Magistrate refused that request, found police investigation unnecessary, and directed the complainant to present evidence under the complaint procedure.
The complainant challenged the Magistrate’s order in revision but did not join the person whose interests were affected.
Without hearing that person, the High Court set aside the Magistrate’s order and directed a preliminary police inquiry.
The Supreme Court found that the Magistrate had applied his mind to the complaint and taken cognizance, and that the High Court’s order could prejudice the absent person.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s order was set aside, and the revision was remitted for the affected person to be joined, heard, and for the matter to be decided afresh.
issues.legal_principle: The requirement of an opportunity to be heard applies to a revisional order prejudicial to an accused or any other person, including at the pre-summoning stage. The Court applied the audi alteram partem principle and the requirement reflected in Section 401(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, relying on Makkapati Nagaswara Sastri v. S.S. Satyanarayan and P. Sundarrajan v. R. Vidhya Sekar. It distinguished Chandra Deo Singh v. Prokash Chandra Bose and Mohd. Yousuf v. Afaq Jahan, and noted that the Magistrate had taken cognizance and proceeded under the complaint procedure.

rule.if: criminal_revision_proceeding and magistrate_applied_mind_to_complaint and revision_order_prejudices_absent_person and absent_person_was_not_given_opportunity_to_be_heard

predicates.criminal_revision_proceeding: The matter is a revision of a Magistrate’s order in a criminal complaint proceeding.
predicates.magistrate_applied_mind_to_complaint: The Magistrate considered the complaint and chose to proceed by examining the complainant or witnesses rather than directing police investigation.
predicates.revision_order_prejudices_absent_person: The revisional court’s order adversely affects a person who was not heard.
predicates.absent_person_was_not_given_opportunity_: The affected person was neither joined nor given an opportunity to present their position before the revisional order was made.

issues.definition: When a Magistrate has considered a complaint and a revisional order would adversely affect an absent person who was not heard, the order requires that person to be heard.
